calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On the power play, Florida is one of the league’s best, but St. Louis is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blues take could cost them.

surprises.head: St. Louis’s power play came alive
surprises.body: St. Louis has one of the league’s least dangerous power plays, and Florida has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Not tonight: St. Louis’s power play created 14.1 expected goals per 60, against their usual 6.4 (about 5.5 against Florida) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Reinhart reaches 700 points as the Panthers beat the Blues
paras: Brady Tkachuk opened the scoring for the Panthers on the power play early in the first, with Sam Reinhart picking up his 700th NHL point on the goal. Dmitry Kulikov extended the lead to 2-0 a little over a minute later, and Anton Lundell pushed the lead to 3-0 early in the second. Reinhart made it 4-0 early in the third. Dylan Holloway got the Blues on the board on the power play with just over two minutes left.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Jacob Markström made 23 saves for the Panthers, and Joel Hofer stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. The Cats moved to 12-7-2, fifth in the Atlantic, while the Blues fell to 9-9-2, seventh in the Central.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Panthers.
Matthew Tkachuk has a point in seven straight games.
Sam Reinhart extended his point streak against St. Louis to six games.
The Panthers’ Radko Gudas played his 900th NHL game.
